articles.title: Is Harry Brook more talented than Kevin Pietersen? Have your say after Ben Stokes hails England white-ball captain
articles.summary: Harry Brook slams 114 not out from 49 balls - including 30 runs off one over - in England's thumping win over Sri Lanka in first T20; Sky Sports' Eoin Morgan says Brook is  producing "genius time and time again in all formats" - watch second T20 on Sky Sports on Thursday (6.30pm start)
articles.body:
Brook is, in many ways, this generation's Pietersen.

A batter with jaw-dropping ability who can take any bowling attacking apart and make accessing any part of the ground look routine but also prone to driving fans mad with a daft dismissal.

In Southampton on Tuesday, though, we only saw the best of Brook as he tonked a 42-ball hundred - England's second-fastest in T20Is - against Sri Lanka, with his 10 fours and half a dozen sixes including six boundaries in one over off Dunith Wellalage.

The swashbuckling innings was played in front of England legend Pietersen, who has joined head coach Brendon McCullum's white-ball set-up as a mentor, up to and including the 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in late 2027.

And Brook's knock lured Stokes onto social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

Stokes, on the day he struck a half-century for Durham against Worcestershire in the County Championship , wrote: "I don't even think the genius of KP could come close to what Brook has talent-wise. You are an absolute freak, Harry. You're mint to watch."

Shortly after, former Test captain Stokes added: "Bit harsh on KP actually. Both are freak talents but Brook is better in my opinion."

So, who do you think is the most talented of the two? Vote in the poll below.

Brook still has a long way to go to match Pietersen longevity-wise.

KP amassed almost 14,000 international runs between 2004 and 2014, a number he was prevented from adding to after a fallout with the ECB truncated his England career.

Brook has over 6,500 international runs since debuting in 2022, so, all being well will eclipse Pietersen's haul at some stage.

At 27, he could have over a decade left - and he hopes to use Pietersen's expertise to become even better.

Brook hopes 'hero' KP can have 'big impact' on his career

Brook said of Pietersen, after revealing he had watched highlights of his innings before Tuesday's T20: "He looked at batting slightly differently, in a similar way to me as well.

"He always wants to put the bowlers under pressure.

"He was a phenomenal player. The way he accessed different areas of the ground made it really tricky to captain and bowl to, and I'm looking forward to conversations about that.

"I mentioned to him earlier about trying to help me read surfaces and using my skills to perform on that pitch as well, not just for white-ball cricket, Test cricket as well.

"Hopefully he can have a big impact on my career. He's a hero to a lot of players. We grew up watching him and it's just awesome to have a man of his calibre in the changing room."

'Genius Brook has everything as a batter'

Brook's sizzling century against Sri Lanka was his first in any international cricket since a T20 ton versus Pakistan in February, during a World Cup match in Pallekele.

It was worth the wait. The batter's picking up of length was extraordinary in an innings highly praised by Sky Sports pundits Eoin Morgan and Kumar Sangakkara.

Sangakkara said of Brook: "He reads length so quickly. He is very light and nimble on his feet. He has oodles of time and devastating power. On the back foot against spin, he is very good at hitting over long-on, long-off, even square.

"Then against the pace there is the scoop and reverse paddle or punch down the ground for six. He has everything."

Morgan added: "I think Harry is one of our very best. It is difficult to find a player of recent generations that has Brook's ability.

"He is coming into his peak years, yet we are seeing absolute genius time and time again in all formats of the game."

Brook's last Test ton may have come over a year ago, against India at The Kia Oval, but he has knuckled down in red-ball matches of late, batting far more responsibly while notching five fifties across the summer in the international game's longest form.

In the international game's shortest form on Tuesday night, he did get a hundred - and how.

He can now chat about it with KP, a bloke he may even have more talent than…

articles.title: County Championship: Leicestershire hit with 27-point deduction and £5,000 fine for breaching pitch regulations
articles.summary: Leicestershire given 27-point deduction and £5,000 fine for breaching pitch regulations in August; Groundsman blamed pitch condition on Bollywood film shoot, but defence dismissed; Watch England's second T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm on Thursday
articles.body:
In a statement on Wednesday, Leicestershire said: "The club notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision, which imposes an eight-point deduction, an additional eight-point deduction suspended until the end of the 2027 season, and a financial penalty of £5,000.

"Under ECB Rothesay County Championship Playing Condition 16.2.6, the 19 points earned in the match concerned will also be deducted from Leicestershire CCC's 2026 Rothesay County Championship total.

"Accordingly, the club will lose 27 points overall.

"Having received the panel's decision, the club is reviewing its position and considering all available options. No further statement will be issued at this time."

The independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) upheld the Cricket Regulator's charge against Leicestershire for breaching the ECB Pitch Regulations, with the pitch at Uptonsteel Grace Road rated as 'poor' during the County Championship match against Glamorgan, between August 20-23.

Leicestershire won the low-scoring match by 42 runs and the pitch was inspected immediately after.

Leicestershire's groundsman Callum Lewin had argued filming of an unscheduled Bollywood film - believed to be for a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly - had taken place at the ground four days before the Glamorgan fixture, preventing the pitch from being covered for eight hours in bright sunshine.

This was dismissed by the panel as a mitigating factor as it was only one day.

In a full written judgment, match referee Ian Ramage logged 43 examples of uneven bounce in the match. The pitch had an unusual look, with a green middle (16mm of grass) to help seamers and bare ends (just 3mm) to help spinners. Other pitches at Grace Road this year have had a similar look and played differently.

The Regulator acknowledged Leicestershire would not have deliberately created a pitch to bounce so unevenly but stated "each of these factors presented foreseeable risks that should have informed part of the planning and preparation process."

In conclusion, the tribunal found that, while Leicestershire did not intend for the pitch to play unevenly, their approach to preparing it was unreasonable. "Accordingly, and for these reasons, LCCC have failed to discharge the burden upon them under Regulation 7.6 that it "sought, acting reasonably, to prepare the best quality pitch that it could for the match that was being staged".

If the Foxes fail to beat Hampshire in their ongoing home game, their return to Division Two will be confirmed.

But they face a tough task to do so after Hampshire closed day two on 255-3 in their second innings - a lead of 225.

articles.title: India's Abhishek Sharma hits 30-ball hundred, the fastest in T20 internationals by batter from Test-playing nation
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma's hundred eclipses the 33-ball T20I centuries scored by Finn Allen of New Zealand and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza; Abhishek powers 11 sixes and nine fours against Afghanistan in Delhi; Rohit Sharma had hit India's previous fastest T20I ton, off 35 balls versus Sri Lanka
articles.body:
Abhishek, who slammed 11 sixes and nine fours in his 108 from 34 deliveries, eclipsed the 33-ball centuries of New Zealand's Finn Allen and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza.

Allen's ton came against South Africa in the T20 World Cup semi-final in Kolkata earlier this year, with Raza's hundred hit against Gambia in Nairobi in October 2024.

Having trumped Allen, Abhishek's hundred is also the quickest in a T20 international between two Test-playing countries.

The fastest men's T20I hundred was scored off 27 balls by Estonia's Sahil Chauhan, against Cyprus in 2024, with Muhammad Fahad doing so from 29 balls for Turkey against Bulgaria a year later, leaving Abhishek third on the overall list.

The quickest hundred in women's T20 internationals was scored by West Indies' Deandra Dottin - a 38-ball effort versus South Africa in St Kitts during the 2010 World Cup.

Abhishek's 30-ball ton not even his fastest in T20s

Abhishek, whose innings on Thursday powered India to 221-7 before Afghanistan folded to 94 all out in reply to suffer a 3-0 series defeat, now has three T20 international tons, the third-most by an Indian after Rohit Sharma (5) and Suryakumar Yadav (4).

Rohit had hit India's previous fastest T20I century, from 35 balls against Sri Lanka in Indore in 2017.

Abhishek has notched an even speedier hundred in domestic T20 cricket, off 28 balls for Punjab against Meghalaya in 2024.

In Afghanistan's failed run chase in this final T20, Abhishek took a catch at deep midwicket.to remove Sediq Atal on the slog sweep.

Nitish Kumar Reddy bagged three wickets in the 12th over as India rolled their opponents in 14.1 overs for a 127-run victory and a series sweep.

articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Nasser Hussain says new white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen could be key for 'second coming' of Tom Banton
articles.summary: Nasser Hussain praises Tom Banton and says the effect new white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen could have on him will be key to England's success; watch the third T20 from Old Trafford on Saturday live on Sky Sports Cricket from 2:30pm
articles.body:
Banton top-scored for England with an unbeaten 52 off 24 balls in an impressive innings, combining well with skipper Harry Brook (23 off 8) after Jos Buttler (30 off 16) had become the first player to make 15,000 T20 runs - as the home side sauntered past Sri Lanka's modest 145-9 with 7.5 overs to spare.

The half-century was Banton's third since re-entering the white-ball set-up as a middle-order batter, having played as an opener in his early career - a transition Hussain lauded on Sky Sports.

"Banton has been really good in his second coming [after moving from opener to the middle order]," said Hussain.

"Everyone talks about what [white-ball mentor] Kevin Pietersen can do for Harry Brook, but I think Pietersen could be good for Banton.

"KP raved about Banton when he came through at Somerset but then he fell away and KP made a couple of comments saying he had to work hard.

"He has worked hard and we are now seeing the rewards of that. KP will now be saying, 'keep improving'. That's what great players do."

Sky Sports Cricket's Kumar Sangakkara also praised Banton's development, adding: "He was just exceptional. Anything that was pitched full, he cleared his front leg. Anything that was on the stumps, straight down the ground.

"Even with pace, he's got that power and that timing to really make a difference. I think he was exceptional. His development, especially against spin, has been brilliant for England."

Hussain was also complimentary of Liam Dawson's performance after the spinner took 3-32 in Sri Lanka's innings, including a crucial two wickets in two balls when the tourists' openers were going well - an impact that Hussain felt changed the course of the match.

"England just outplayed Sri Lanka in every department," Hussain added. "At 55-0 after five [overs], you thought Sri Lanka are actually going to put on a showing here and maybe test England.

"But it was Liam Dawson with two in an over [that changed the course of the match] - and on a ground where sometimes bowling spin isn't easy and sides often leave out their spinner.

"He's a very smart cricketer. He's a very tough cricketer and he's been around a long time. And he'll know what sort of lengths and lines to bowl on this particular ground. So that was brilliant from Dawson."

The defeat was Sri Lanka's 14th in succession against England in T20 internationals - a record which was indicative to Hussain of a larger malaise in comparison to past sides.

"Sri Lanka are just way off the side that I've seen over the years - just way off," he said.

"It's a massive drop off in the batting in particular. I've watched some of their greats and they're just strokers of the ball. They stroke the ball for six, for four - but what I see at the moment is people trying to over hit.

"On good pitches, last game, this game, the moment there was a bit of pace, they're losing their shape.

"In every metric today, England completely outplayed them. There were 50 dot balls. Ten sixes England scored, [and Sri Lanka scored] two sixes, even with these straight boundaries.

"A coach or a director of cricket or whoever will look at and sit back and go, that wasn't good enough - and when you're playing against England, those metrics have to be closer together.

articles.summary: Somerset lose leadership of Division One to Warwickshire heading into the final round of matches after hugely-costly 185-run defeat to Yorkshire at Headingley; Somerset at home to Surrey, while Warwickshire host Leicestershire in final title-deciding matches from September 24
articles.body:
Top of the County Championship Division One table heading into the penultimate round of matches, Somerset saw rivals Warwickshire wrap up a two-day victory against Essex but failed to keep pace at Headingley.

Chasing 287 - the highest score of the match - they were bundled out for 101 on the final day. Resuming on 73-3 they collapsed horribly as their final seven wickets fell for 25 runs in less than 13 overs.

Ben Cliff took three of them as he finished with 3-29 after taking 8-76 in the first innings, while Ben Coad claimed 4-33 and Matthew Revis 2-7.

The 185-run defeat leaves Somerset chasing from behind heading into their season-ending fixture against Surrey and one step further away from ending their 135-year quest for the county game's top prize.

Warwickshire will take an 11-point lead into the final round with Nottinghamshire also suffering a heavy defeat, while Hampshire have been relegated.

Notts could only set Sussex 76 to win at Hove and, although they grabbed a couple of early wickets to reduce the hosts to 14-2, Sussex secured a seven-wicket win just after the lunch break.

Warwickshire top the table on 203 points and need only to beat Leicestershire in their final game of the season at Edgbaston to be crowned champions for the first time since 2021.

Hampshire's five-wicket defeat by Leicestershire means they are relegated to Division Two.

Leicestershire, deducted 27 points for a breach of ECB pitch regulations earlier this week, will join them if they fail to beat Warwickshire and even a win might not be enough if Essex secure six points against Glamorgan.

articles.title: Brydon Carse: No charges against England cricketer after police close investigation into alleged assault at nightclub
articles.summary: Derbyshire Police have ended their investigation into an alleged assault incident which involved England and Durham cricketer Brydon Carse; Carse, who has played for Durham in the County Championship during the investigation over the last month, will not face any charges
articles.body:
Last month, Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series against Pakistan.

The 31-year-old was celebrating with Durham players after their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship and was also seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background.

In a statement, Derbyshire Police said: "An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

"Officers attended Molly Malones in the Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday 23 August. A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers."

Subsequent enquiries were made pursuing the allegations of an assault but, after the alleged victim was identified and spoken to, no further action was taken, police said.

The matter is now in the hands of the independent Cricket Regulator, which will assess if Carse has a disciplinary issue to answer to relating to his conduct.

Sky Sports News has contacted the England and Wales Cricket Board for comment.

Carse has continued playing for Durham since the episode took place, helping his side win the Division Two title of the Rothesay County Championship, but he has been overlooked by England.

He was immediately removed from the squad ahead of the second Test against Pakistan, then left out of the final match too. While officially considered available for selection for the ongoing white-ball series against Sri Lanka, he was left on the sidelines once again.

Speaking earlier this week, England's limited-overs head coach Brendon McCullum called for his side to be mindful of their off-field responsibilities and added: "I've spoken to Carsey a lot and it's the same message - you need to make good decisions off the field that allow you to be able to be the best version of yourself.

"As far as Carsey is concerned, it's a good chance for him now to get his house in order and then push for selection for the next opportunity that arises."

Test captain Joe Root also had his say ahead of the Lord's Test when he described himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

On Carse, he said: "I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself."

articles.title: England hammer Sri Lanka to return top of T20 world rankings as 3-0 series sweep clinched at Emirates Old Trafford
articles.summary: Jos Buttler smacks unbeaten 62 off 32 balls as England chase 125-run target in only 9.4 overs to make it 15 T20 international wins in a row over Sri Lanka; watch the first ODI between the two teams on Tuesday from 12pm, live on Sky Sports Cricket (first ball 12.30pm)
articles.body:
Off the back of 119-run and six-wicket wins in the opening two games, Harry Brook's side clinched a 3-0 series sweep as his 33 off 21 balls, plus Jos Buttler's unbeaten 62 off 32 fired the hosts to their 125-run target in a mere 9.4 overs.

Aneurin Donald (13 off 6) could only manage a brief cameo with the bat for the third time in the series - stumped off Tharindu Ratnayake - while Brook was run out just shy of victory, one that Buttler clinched with a stunning one-handed six over deep midwicket to make it 15 wins in a row for England against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals.

The visitors had earlier been bowled out for a paltry 124 in 18.5 overs after being inserted by England, with Sonny Baker (2-17), Jofra Archer (2-23) and Will Jacks (2-31) picking up a couple apiece as the wickets were generously shared around.

Pathum Nissanka (36 off 24) had briefly given cause for optimism - despite the early wickets of Lahiru Udara (10), to a strong catch from Buttler in the swirling wind, and Kamil Mishara (2) - as he cleared the rope on three occasions in the opening powerplay.

Nissanka was a touch unlucky to ultimately perish in the seventh over, with Brook taking a terrific, diving catch at midwicket off one nailed out of the middle of the Sri Lankan opener's bat.

Skipper Charith Asalanka's innings was a sedentary 16 off 14 deliveries before being run out by Jacks - only just - after he nearly missed the stumps altogether with his take at the non-striker's end.

Kamindu Mendis (35 off 28) struck a couple of heavy-handed blows, but he too was lacking in support and the Sri Lankan collapse was well and truly in force by the time he picked out Jacks on the deep midwicket fence.

The tourists lost their last six wickets for 17 runs in less than five overs, with Wanindu Hasaranga's dismal departure - hit wicket off Archer after nearly swinging himself off his feet - pretty symptomatic of Sri Lanka's struggles in the series.

And they have got little time to rectify things for the three-match one-day international series which follows and gets under way in Durham on Tuesday.

Brook: No 1 ranking an 'amazing' achievement

England captain and player of the series Harry Brook :

"Being back at world No 1 in T20s is an amazing achievement and one everyone should be really proud of.

"Everyone stepped up, especially lads who haven't played as much.

"For Sonny Baker to bowl three overs in the powerplay in two games is an amazing achievement, not going for many runs and taking wickets.

"We want to be a side when the conditions aren't in our favour where we are still able to manufacture a win.

"That might not be the prettiest but we are doing it extremely well and are trending in the right direction."

"England have been superb. They look a much better team than Sri Lanka but look well-oiled and seem to know what they are doing.

"Even players you might not feel are in the best 11 - remember, England are missing Phil Salt, Sam Curran and Jacob Bethell through injury - appear like they know what they are doing.

"With clear roles and responsibility, you get good performances and that's what nearly every player has produced in this series."

articles.title: Metro Bank One Day Cup women's final: The Blaze beat Hampshire in final-ball thriller to secure domestic treble
articles.summary: Emma Jones hit an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls for The Blaze and scored the winning runs off the final ball of the match in Southampton after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had recorded half-centuries against Hampshire for whom Ella McCaughan top-scored with 78
articles.body:
The Trent Bridge-based side had already lifted the Vitality Blast and Vitality T20 County Cup but were forced to dig deep after needing 17 from the last two overs and then two off the final ball. Emma Jones was the hero with an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls and scored the winning runs - after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had scored half-centuries in the chase of 252.

Earlier, Lucy Higham had taken 4-49 to help restrict Hampshire - who were also losing finalists in 2025 - to 251, with Ella McCaughan and Freya Kemp whacking fifties in vein. The Blaze won the toss and, through the miserliness of Grace Ballinger and Charley Phillips, only allowed 11 runs in the first five overs. But Hampshire's opening pair of the super-in-form Maia Bouchier and McCaughan slowly began to turn the tide in their direction with an 84-run stand. McCaughan confidently pinged the ball around for her first fifty since June.

Bouchier, who was dropped on a duck, could not make it three centuries in a row when she holed out to long-on before Georgia Adams slapped straight to mid-off shortly afterwards - both to Higham. The hosts kicked back as McCaughan and Kemp dominated the middle overs with a 67-run stand and were 166-2 in the 32nd over. But The Blaze used their final nous to pull things back. Higham added wickets three and four of the afternoon by having Kemp stumped and Naomi Dattani caught brilliantly by Kirstie Gordon at mid-on. The spinner has taken 14 wickets in eight matches since her return from The Hundred - with this 4-49, her third four-for in that period. Pacer Phillips dismissed Rhianna Southby, Abi Norgrove and Amanda-Jade Wellington in three overs in a row, as Hampshire slumped and could only reach 251.

In response, Sarah Bryce and Beaumont made mincemeat of the bowlers for 15 overs, as they strode towards the target. The pair put on 95 with relative ease, and then Wellington spun things by seeing off both Bryce sisters in an over - Sarah was caught at deep square before Kathryn was superbly caught at slip. Beaumont, with the help of Elwiss, kept things ticking, although the former England opener lived a charmed life - she was dropped three times and also survived a stumping chance. Her luck ran out, having scored her fifth half-century of the campaign, when she was lbw to Wellington - sparking three wickets to fall in 26 balls. And with 30 still needed, Gordon was caught. It meant there was 17 required from the last two overs, but Jones took the sting out of things. A ridiculous reverse pull and a straight drive both went to the boundary, and despite a run out with the third ball, Jones took her side to victory with a swept four off the final ball of a nerve-filled match.

articles.title: Stephen Fleming: England's new head coach targets No 1 spot in Test rankings but says 'work to be done' on discipline
articles.summary: Stephen Fleming says he has had "a lot of contact" with Test captain Joe Root during the Pakistan series and has spoken with former skipper Ben Stokes following his international retirement earlier this summer; "Ben's happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision", he said
articles.body:
In June, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended from the second Test of the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand due to a nightclub incident that occurred in the wake of their opening win at Lord's.

Last month, Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series whitewash of Pakistan, prompting Test captain Joe Root to describe himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

Carse did not face any charges after police closed their investigation.

"It's disappointing," Fleming said. "The way that players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me."

He added: "I watched Joe in the press conference, and when he voices his displeasure at the behaviour, I think that said it all.

"If you want a great example of how to behave as an international cricketer, Joe Root is it.

"There's work to be done, and that comes back to making sure we're tying into something a bit bigger than oneself."

As well as having "a lot of contact" with Root since accepting the Test job on July 30 and throughout the Pakistan series - which Fleming was not yet in post for, due to family and commercial commitments - the new coach said he had also been in touch with Stokes, who retired from international cricket in June.

Amid suggestions of a possible return for the home Ashes series next summer, Fleming said of the 35-year-old: "He's really happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision.

"My view is that when a player decides to retire, it's a big decision, and I have the utmost respect for that decision."

Fleming excited for Ashes and keen to take England to top

Fleming admitted he is already excited about coaching England in next summer's Ashes, calling it "an absolute highlight", while he also talked up the potential of the team he is about to take over.

"I would love to be in charge of the number one Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration," Fleming said.

"My honest appraisal is it's a great time to be the head coach. I think it's a real opportunity with the players that are coming through.

"The fast bowlers as an example, I loved watching them operate in the [Pakistan] Test series recently.

"Also, the introduction of [Jordan] Cox and [Dan] Lawrence was nice, when you've got someone like [Jacob] Bethell [to come back].

"There's talent there competing for places, and that's always the barometer. If you're leaving very good players out, then you're going to be in a healthy situation."

Fleming added on the World Test Championship, in which England sit sixth in the 2025-2027 cycle - having failed to reach the final of any of the previous three editions: "I think England could do much better in that.

"If that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it, along with every other marquee event that comes our way?

"That opportunity is real, but there's a huge amount of work to do."

Fleming rejects 'Flemball' in pursuit of 'cricket sense'

As for the playing style Fleming will look for his team to adopt, he was keen to praise the prior work of Stokes and former New Zealand team-mate - England's current white-ball coach - Brendon McCullum, but said he is looking to "combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments".

There will be no 'Bazball' style moniker to accompany his team's style, however, as per his predecessor.

"That's a medical condition," Fleming joked when presented with the prospect of 'Flemball'.

"The way they [Stokes and McCullum] changed the nature of Test cricket was quite remarkable, and I have a huge amount of respect for the courage that that took.

"Obviously, the last 12 months it hasn't evolved as they would have liked and the fans would have liked, but I still acknowledge that period of two years [prior]."

He added: "I really loved the positive play and the freeing up of the England players, so if I could take that and combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments.

"There are key times in a match that you have to be really smart, and maybe we can just work a bit harder on that - but still combine positive nature of the players that are in there."

Root is 'greatness' and 'the best guy to captain Test team'

Talking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast , Fleming elaborated further on the respect he has for Root and how delighted he is to have him as captain of the Test team.

Root had previously captained England from 2017-2022 before being replaced by Stokes following a barren run of one win in his last 17 Tests.

Upon Stokes' resignation, white-ball skipper Harry Brook could have been an all-format option, but Fleming is thrilled that Root accepted the role again.

"I am a really big fan of Root," Fleming said. "I think he is a wonderful player and ambassador for the game, so to work with him was really appealing.

"I just knew that he is the best guy to captain this side. He epitomises everything that is great about an international player. He is greatness, but a wonderful human being in the way that he conducts himself and can go about being great.

"He is such a great role model and such a perfect person for a young group of players. It was a no-brainer, for me, for him to be captain.

"Root is in charge. If he is going out and making key decisions, he is in charge. My role is very closely linked to provide him with what he needs. That can be criticism, constructively, so it's not just a yes position.

"I want him to be the best he can be and I think there is still room to grow in his captaincy with this group. I don't necessarily know what that looks like but I know there is growth and that's exciting."

articles.title: Stephen Fleming: Stuart Broad excited at what new England Test cricket coach can do for Joe Root's captaincy
articles.summary: Sky Sports pundit Stuart Broad on Stephen Fleming-Joe Root relationship: "Where Joe needs a bit of help with his captaincy is taking a bit of weight off his shoulders at times, allowing him to concentrate on batting, make tactical decisions and get feedback throughout to help England out"
articles.body:
Fleming was named as countryman Brendon McCullum's successor in late July but did not lead the side for the recent 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to family commitments.

The 53-year-old recently flew to England for a short trip to chat with ECB officials and Test skipper Root as well as the counties, and was with the national team as they completed a 3-0 T20I whitewash under white-ball coach McCullum in Manchester on Saturday .

Fleming - who has never been a head coach in red-ball cricket before but has extensive franchise-league experience, chiefly with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL - spoke to media ahead of the final T20I, including to Michael Atherton for the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast.

Broad said after listening to former New Zealand captain Fleming's chat with Atherton, in which he lauded Root: "What struck me was his love of leadership.

"He spoke a lot about that and strategy rather than really intricate coaching, so I am assuming he will pass a lot of the technique coaching on to his bowling coach, batting coach etc, which is what they are there to do.

'Root needs feedback Fleming will give him'

"I think what excites me is him working with Root's captaincy.

"Fleming was a good captain and has worked a lot with MS Dhoni at Chennai. He has learnt about tactical stuff on the field and how to manage changing rooms as well.

"Where Joe needs, or would like, a bit of help with his captaincy is taking a bit of weight off his shoulders at times, allowing him to just concentrate on his batting, make some tactical decisions and get feedback throughout the game to help England out.

"Joe hasn't naturally got a bowling attack that will feed back a lot of tactical advice so I think he needs that.

"As a coach you are very reliant on your captain. Fleming has had a very good one in Dhoni and maybe not quite clicked with others he tried to have success with.

"But the way he talked about Root, I imagine he will click with him."

Broad does not view this being Fleming's first red-ball head coach role as an issue.

"He loved playing the game, he loves studying and coaching the game, so you love all formats," said the former England seamer.

"He made his name in Test match cricket and I have no doubt he has watched and been around current players."

'England need leaders to start winning Test series'

When Ben Stokes quit internationals at the end of the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer, there were few options to replace him as captain besides Root - who first led England between 2017 and 2022 - and white-ball skipper Harry Brook.

Broad says a key part of Fleming's remit is to develop more leaders as England look to return to the peak of Test cricket, having not won any of the four five-match series they played against either Australia or India in the Bazball era.

The pundit added: "Fleming has a group that is exciting but England have also lost a lot of cricket over the last 18 months, so he has some moulding to do.

"A big problem for this team has been the lack of leaders and you can see it on the field.

"I don't really mind a lack of leaders to choose as captain when you have Root and Brook as options but on the field there has been a stark problem.

"Fleming has noticed that and will focus on that. He will drop nuggets of information in consistently throughout to try and build leadership. We need leaders to start winning Test series."

articles.title: How one India T20I could become Japanese cricket's defining moment
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Associ.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Association (JCA) COO pulled covers off the wicket. Later, he was putting up hospitality tents, checking security plans and helping transform a quaint cricket ground with 500 permanent seats into a venue worthy of hosting the reigning T20I world champions. By Tuesday, weather permitting, India will walk out against Japan in the country's first-ever men's senior international against a Full Member.For Japanese cricket, getting here is success in itself and the scoreline almost secondary."A lot of success has almost already happened," Curr says. "The fact that India have agreed to come, the fact that I'm sitting here talking to you guys, the fact that Japanese media are coming to learn about cricket — we're having successes already," he told select media.Cricket is not new to Japan, having been introduced in the 1870s. But adaptation is a different story. Baseball, Football, Sumo Wrestling, Basketball, Golf, Tennis, Boxing are some sports that are bigger. India's arrival represents cricket's loudest introduction in recent memory.More than just another T20I matchJapan has played in Under-19 World Cups, faced India and Pakistan at youth level and competed in the Asian Games with its women's team. But this is different gravy."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan," Curr says. "It's piquing interest, but we've still got a long way to go before cricket breaks into the mainstream sporting audience."That mainstream audience is precisely what the JCA hopes to reach. The timing is ideal: cricket returns to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya just days later, allowing Japan to explain the sport through one of the country's most recognisable sporting events."The Asian Games gives cricket legitimacy that it didn't have before," Curr says. "You can't be what you can't see."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan.Cricket's quiet, but slow, growth in JapanBehind the scenes, cricket has been expanding steadily in Japan. Registered players have risen from around 3,000 when Curr arrived in 2014 to 8,800 today. The Japan Cup -- the T20 competition in the country -- has grown from barely a dozen teams to more than 80, while the domestic 40-over league now spans four divisions."Kaizen is the word," Curr says. "Continual improvement. That's what we're trying to do for the sport. But now and again there are moments like this where you can accelerate that," he added.Winning hearts and viewers, not necessarily the matchJapan harbour no illusions about the cricketing challenge ahead. "This India team is pretty good," Curr said as a matter of fact. "It's going to be an extremely difficult challenge for players who have never played at that level before."Instead, his measure of success is cultural.He points to Japan's women's team, praised recently for staying back after their Asian Games fixture against India to thank supporters and mingle with fans. That's the identity he wants the men's side to showcase too."We want cricket to be played hard but also be accessible and friendly," he says. "We want cricket to be fun."If thousands of first-time spectators leave Sano remembering more than just India's star power, Japanese cricket may have achieved exactly what it came for.The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCAHow India fixture came into beingThe historic fixture was never part of Japan's grand plan to expand the sport. It began with clay.Eighteen months ago, the JCA set out to relay the turf square at Sano with help from Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC), whose groundsman travelled to Japan to identify suitable clay. The same surface was eventually used to build the Asian Games venue in Nagoya, prompting a simple thought: if Japan had international-quality wickets, why not invite the world's best teams to use them?Once the pitches were completed in March, Japan prepared a proposal and sent it to every Full Member ahead of the ICC conference in Edinburgh. Conversations with the BCCI began there — and, to Curr's surprise, moved quickly."The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCA," he said.The timing made sense. With the Asian Games beginning days later, India men's squad would otherwise spend nearly a week waiting for their knockout fixture without access to proper cricket facilities. Sano offered both a training base and, eventually, a match. Again, with fingers crossed that the weather doesn't play spoilsport.India vs Japan T20I will be broadcast LIVE on FanCode on September 22 at 9:30 am IST.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: BENGALURU: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is set to introduce a policy defining the scope of the Ombudsman and preventing its office from entertaining complaints concerning local or state-level matters, the TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The move is understood to aim at drawing a clearer line between issues that fall within the Ombudsman’s jurisdiction and those that the respective state associations should address first. articles.title: One-Day Cup final: Middlesex beat Leicestershire by 31 runs
articles.summary: Middlesex claim their first silverware in a decade as they beat Leicestershire in a thrilling One-Day Cup final.
articles.body:
Metro Bank Men's One-Day Cup final, Trent Bridge

Middlesex 231 (49.5 overs): Higgins 100, Duke 55; Holland 5-36

Leicestershire 200 (44.2 overs): Kelly 103; Roland-Jones 3-27, Helm 3-32

Middlesex claimed their first silverware in a decade as they fought back from a tricky start to beat Leicestershire in a thrilling One-Day Cup final at Trent Bridge.

Having been put into bat by Leicestershire captain Stephen Eskinazi, Ryan Higgins' magnificent hundred dug Middlesex out of a hole and helped them reach 231 before being bowled out in the final over of their innings.

Higgins, 31, struck nine fours in his 115-ball knock after his team had slumped to 71-5 in the 22nd over, putting on 135 with on-loan Yorkshire wicketkeeper Harry Duke (55) for the sixth wicket.

Ian Holland returned his second-best List-A figures of 5-36 for the Foxes, while England all-rounder Rehan Ahmed took 3-55.

In reply, Leicestershire too lost early wickets as former England seamer Toby Roland-Jones bowled 10 overs straight through in a fine opening spell of 3-27.

Leicestershire were indebted to the efforts of New Zealand international Nick Kelly, who reached a glorious century of his own off 103 deliveries and appeared to be taking his side to victory.

However, the game swung again in the over after Kelly reached his hundred as the left-hander heaved Tom Helm to Higgins on the mid-wicket fence to leave Leicestershire eight down.

And that proved the decisive moment as Helm dismissed Ajaz Patel and Tom Scriven skied Naavya Sharma straight up, with captain Ben Geddes taking the winning catch.

Middlesex's most recent success was the County Championship in 2016, and they had not won a white-ball trophy since lifting the T20 Blast in 2008.

Higgins & Roland-Jones star as Middlesex end drought

Middlesex had to overcome adversity more than once in Nottingham as they ended their long wait for a trophy.

They faced the most difficult batting conditions of the day in the opening hour and many teams would have crumbled at 71-5.

The sixth-wicket partnership between Higgins and Duke was a game-defining one as they fought back and gave their bowlers something to work with.

It was Higgins' first List-A hundred and it will live long in the memory for Middlesex supporters fortunate enough to watch it as he displayed character, graft and no shortage of skill.

Roland-Jones is a legendary figure at the club and he showed exactly why with a near-immaculate spell, taking the key scalps of Rishi Patel and Ahmed.

Sharma is Middlesex's leading wicket-taker in this competition and the 21-year-old too impressed with the ball, making the breakthrough as he found Eskinazi's outside edge, pinning Hamza Shaikh lbw and then returning to take the final wicket.

With Kelly in full flow, heads never went down and they showed all the composure of a team that have only lost once in this format all season.

Off the back of their 27-point deduction in the County Championship , Leicestershire's team talk is more than likely to have been straightforward.

And they started like a team with a point to prove after Eskinazi won the toss, backed by a vocal travelling support.

Holland set the tone with the new ball, nicking off Nathan Fernandes and Max Holden cheaply before Tom Scriven took two wickets of his own, including a fine catch by wicketkeeper Ben Cox to remove Josh De Caires (26).

Incredibly Cox caught the first five wickets to fall.

Middlesex fought back through Higgins and Duke, and the Foxes will perhaps look back on that partnership as an opportunity that slipped away.

Rishi Patel and Eskinazi got the chase off to a bright start, but three wickets for just three runs stalled their momentum and similarly to Middlesex's innings, Leicestershire found themselves five wickets down in the 70s.

Ahmed will regret his decision not to review after being given out lbw off Roland-Jones, with replays showing it would have missed leg stump.

Much as Higgins revived Middlesex, Kelly breathed new life into the Leicestershire chase with his defiant knock, which featured 10 fours and three sixes.

The Kiwi left-hander was being serenaded from the stands as the runs required ticked away, but he had to drag himself from the middle with 44 runs still needed.

Those fans continued to sing until the end, but were left disappointed as their team fell short.

articles.title: Metro Bank One Day Cup men's final: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait
articles.summary: Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls at Trent Bridge, playing a starring role as Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final
articles.body:
Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.

Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

Leicestershire, still reeling from the points deduction in the Rothesay County Championship that makes relegation almost certain, had hoped to ease the pain winning a second Metro Bank trophy in the space of four seasons but it was not to be.

Put in, Middlesex were 32-3 in the 11th over and five down in the 22nd - all snared by the immaculate Cox.

Nathan Fernandes slashed at one from Holland, who dismissed Max Holden in similar fashion, and Tom Scriven found a thin edge to remove skipper Ben Geddes for a duck.

Josh De Caires fell victim to a superb leg-side grab before Luke Hollman nicked a first-ball googly from Rehan Ahmed and Cox celebrated again.

But Duke - on loan from Yorkshire as cover for the injured Joe Cracknell - provided the support Higgins needed before a top edge to extra cover brought his undoing, Helm was leg before to Rehan and Higgins perished one ball after going to his maiden List A hundred, failing to clear long-on, looking for a 10th boundary.

The Leicestershire innings almost exactly mirrored that of Middlesex as they slipped to 32-3 and 79-5. Sharma dismissed Foxes captain and former Middlesex batter Stephen Eskinazi, caught at second slip, and Hamza Shaikh leg before, veteran Roland-Jones having Rishi Patel caught at deep square leg.

Roland-Jones claimed two more victims in Ahmed, leg before, and Cox, caught behind.

Leicestershire found themselves needing someone to step up as Higgins had and Kelly answered the call. Allowing few scoring opportunities to pass him by, reaching 50 from 52 balls with six fours and a pick-up for six off Sharma as he and Holland added 50 for the sixth wicket.

Ben Green's departure added more pressure, with 57 still needed. Kelly, who twice hammered Zafar down the ground for more sixes, kept the Foxes in the hunt, reaching 100 from 103 balls.

But, after needing treatment for cramp, he pulled Helm straight to deep square. Ajaz Patel fell to a stunning catch at backward point by Zafar off Helm, before Scriven was the last man to go, caught at mid-off.

articles.title: Gavin Williams dominates with 7 shutout frames as Guardians edge Athletics to stay atop AL Central
articles.summary: Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the A...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the AL Central.

Steven Kwan added three hits for Cleveland, which posted its seventh series sweep of the season and third at home.

The Guardians (81-75) are 1 1/2 games in front of the Chicago White Sox . They finish the season on the road with series against Boston and Kansas City .

Williams (14-8) gave up three hits and struck out nine to move into the major-league lead with 244 strikeouts. He has one more than Milwaukee 's Jacob Misiorowski . Toronto 's Dylan Cease is in third with 239. It is the 13th time in 31 starts this season that the right-hander has had at least nine strikeouts.

Cade Smith worked 1 1/3 innings for his 39th save in 44 opportunities.

The Athletics were swept for the second straight series and lost all six games on their road trip.

José Ramírez led off the fourth with a double down the right-field line, advanced to third on Chase DeLauter 's fly out to left and scored on Jo Adell's infield single. Pitcher Jack Perkins (3-12) fielded the soft grounder on the grass in front of the mound, but his throw hit Adell in the back as he was in the basepath.

Athletics manager Mark Kotsay was ejected for the third time this season for agruing the call.

Perkins went six innings and allowed one run on four hits.

The Athletics' best chance came in the eighth inning when they had runners on second and third with one out. Hunter Gaddis struck out pinch-hitter Carlos Cortes and Smith whiffed Henry Bolte.

Athletics: Return home to face the Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday. LHP Brady Brasso (1-3, 4.50 ERA) will take the mound.

Guardians: LHP Parker Messic (12-9, 2.57 ERA) goes on Tuesday to start a three-game series at Boston.

articles.title: Kade Anderson strong in Mariners 2-1 win in Colorado
articles.summary: Dominic Canzone picks up two key hits as Mariners extend season
articles.body:
Kade Anderson had his best-ever performance, and the Mariners extended their suffering another day.

The Mariners beat the Rockies 2-1 on Sunday in an uneventful game that was neither short nor long, exciting nor boring, meaningful nor insignificant. It was a baseball game between two bad teams, with just enough happening to be better than the offseason ahead. With the win, the Mariners take the series and avoid elimination entering the final week.

Anderson was the selling point for this one. He was fantastic for the first time in the majors. On the one hand, it came against the league's worst offense. On the other, it came at the league's launching pad in Denver. However you prefer to qualify it, Anderson was excellent in a Big League start that counts for real. He threw seven scoreless innings, allowed just three runs hits, and walked none while striking out seven. Most importantly, he got tons of chase out of the zone and picked up a career-high 14 whiffs:

It was good to see. Anderson struggle in his first five starts in the majors, with a 5.33 ERA and 4.44 FIP. He hadn't shown an ability to throw strikes or miss bats or prevent hard contact or keep the ball on the ground. That's not abnormal for a rookie, especially one who threw all of 93 innings in the minors and none above Double-A. But a strong outing Sunday — and hopefully one more against the Angels next week — is a nice confidence booster entering the offseason.

On the other side, the Mariners were getting perfecto'd through three innings, and I was getting a bit nervous that I'd need to put some effort into this recap. Thankfully, they figured out Tomoyuki Sugano in the fourth. Randy Arozarena drew an eight pitch walk, and Dominic Canzone singled up the middle to bring a hustling Arozarena around to score the game's first run. It looked like the Mariners might have a big inning in the works after Cal Raleigh walked, but Julio grounded into a double play to end the threat. The Mariners got a second run in the sixth inning, this time off Ryan Feltner . J.P Crawford singled to lead off, and Canzone doubled him home.

That was it for offense in this one. I'm not really exaggerating. I have listed three of the four hits and two of the three walks the Mariners collected in this one. Lazaro Montes walked in the seventh and Julio picked up an infield single in the ninth, if you want me to be thorough.

I was done with the recap, then Andrés Muñoz gave up a home run to Hunter Goodman in the bottom of the ninth to make it 2-1. After a walk, Dan Wilson came out with the trainer in tow. Muñoz left with an injury, and Eduard Bazardo took over. Bazardo struck out a batter, walked a batter to put the winning run on base, and struck out another batter to end the game.

The Mariners are still technically alive. The Rangers and Astros also lost on Sunday, so their "tragic number" remains at two. That puts the dagger in the hands of the Astros in Seattle next week.

articles.body: From IIT Kanpur to Japan’s national cricket team, Abhishek Anand’s journey has taken an unexpected turn and now, a viral video has put the Bihar-born cricketer in the spotlight ahead of Japan’s historic T20I against India.The 28-year-old, who hails from Bihar’s Rohtas district, moved to Japan for employment after completing his Chemistry degree at IIT Kanpur. He continued pursuing cricket alongside his professional career, eventually earning a place in Japan’s national team.However, despite the buzz surrounding his story, Abhishek’s participation in the September 22 fixture is not confirmed. Japan have announced a 15-member squad for the match, and Abhishek is not among the selected players.From IIT Kanpur to Japan’s cricket circuitDuring his college years in IIT Kanpur, he remained connected to cricket and captained the institute’s team. After graduating, he relocated to Tokyo for work. Rather than giving up the sport, he began playing club cricket in Japan, balancing his professional commitments with his passion for the game.His performances in the local cricket circuit helped him earn a call-up to Japan’s national setup. Abhishek made his T20I debut against the Cook Islands on May 9, 2025. He has since played 18 T20Is, scoring 275 runs, including a highest score of 55, and taking one wicket, according to figures cited in recent reports.‘Bihari Kahan Nahi Hai Bhai’: Abhishek’s video goes viralAbhishek’s journey has attracted attention on social media ahead of the India-Japan fixture, with a video fea turing the cricketer going viral. articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: For the last year or so, Rohit Sharma has gone into every series with growing speculation over his future. The departure of current chief sele.
articles.body: MUMBAI: For the last year or so, Rohit Sharma has gone into every series with growing speculation over his future. The departure of current chief selector Ajit Agarkar - which will become official after October 4, the last date of his tenure - has again turned the spotlight on the former India skipper. It is widely believed that Agarkar's fallout with the BCCI on Rohit's future could be the catalyst in the former India and Mumbai pacer not seeking an extension of his tenure. On September 3, after a review meeting at its headquarters in Mumbai, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia once again sought to quash the uncertainty around Rohit's ODI future.Amidst a raging debate on the issue, former India pacer and chief selector Chetan Sharma has given a thumbs-up to the 39-year-old Rohit continuing to wear India's ODI jersey."I can understand that people are saying a hundred things. I have been a cricketer too, so I respect and love them as cricketers. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are the 'Kohinoors' of Indian cricket. Age is just a number. If they are good, then why not (can they continue). I myself was a selector. Rohit recently scored a century (138 against England at Lord's in third ODI on July 19). Virat, every game he gets one. Then what is the problem? We want players who can win games for us, and they both are capable of doing it," Sharma told TOI on Monday.Sharma, the first bowler to take a hat-trick in ODI World Cup history (in 1987 against New Zealand at Nagpur), confessed that he was a big fan of the superstar batters. "I love watching them when they come and bat for India and they win trophies for us. Rohit won us a trophy after so many years (when he captained India to their second T20 World Cup triumph, and first in 17 years). We should be grateful. We should not listen to other people," Sharma stressed, while talking at an event in Mumbai.Asked specifically if he wished Rohit and Kohli to play in the ODI World Cup next year, Sharma, who played 23 Tests and 65 ODIs from 1984-94, picking up 128 wickets, replied by saying, "If they are fit, they are getting the runs, then why not? I am asking this question to everyone."Considering that presently, Agarkar is apparently not keen to continue because of differences on Rohit's international future, how would Sharma, who was India's chief selector from Dec 2020-Feb 2023, have handled the situation had he been in Agarkar's place? "I won't go into that. When I was the chief selector, we made Rohit the captain. We trusted him, that's why we made him the captain. Virat was always an asset for Indian cricket. As I said, if they are fit, they are getting runs for India, then we should be happy," Sharma asserted.Sharma was pleased that the BCCI has now made it mandatory for all the India players to play domestic cricket as long as they were fit and available. "When I was the India chief selector, my thinking was that if you are doing well in domestic cricket, you should be given a chance. The BCCI spends so much money and effort to organise domestic cricket. We have to respect domestic cricket. Recently, I saw an article that the BCCI told everyone about domestic cricket. So, my dream has come true, and I am really thankful to the BCCI for this. You must play in the Ranji Trophy or first- class cricket if you are fit,” Sharma felt.Sharma, meanwhile, backed both the India women's and men's teams to clinch the gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi Nagoya in Japan. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s preparations for their historic T20 International against Japan were disrupted by rain and stormy conditions on Monday, with Typhoon Dujuan approaching eastern Japan and preventing the Shreyas Iyer-led side from training on the eve of the landmark fixture.The powerful typhoon was moving towards Japan’s Pacific coast, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and an increased risk of landslides across the Kanto region, which includes Tokyo and surrounding areas. The Japan Meteorological Agency warned that conditions could deteriorate rapidly as the storm moved closer to the region.The India squad is based in Japan ahead of Tuesday’s match at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi Prefecture. The fixture, called the Suzuki Cup, marks the first meeting between India and Japan in men’s international cricket and has been organised as part of celebrations marking 75 years of India-Japan diplomatic relations.Typhoon disrupts India's preparationsHeavy rain had already lashed parts of eastern Japan, with the Izu Islands and areas along the Pacific coast recording more than 300 mm of rainfall since Saturday. The weather agency warned that rainfall could intensify as Dujuan approached the Kanto region, while authorities also cautioned about the possibility of linear rain bands capable of triggering flash floods.The weather disruption has also affected the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, with organisers postponing the equestrian eventing competition as a precaution against the approaching storm.For India, the loss of the eve-of-match training session means the players will head into a first-ever international encounter with Japan without a final opportunity to familiarise themselves with the local conditions.That could be particularly relevant given that even captain Iyer admitted the Indian side has limited knowledge of the playing conditions and wicket.Iyer excited despite unfamiliar conditionsSpeaking ahead of the match, Iyer described his experience in Japan so far as "beautiful" and praised the hospitality he and his teammates had received."It is beautiful. I mean, the time we landed, we saw the people very cordial, generous, and helpful in nature, which we see at back at home as well. The hospitality is brilliant, and yeah, I mean, it is too early to talk about it, but I'm sure that I've heard special things from people about Japan as a country and Tokyo as a city as well, so looking forward to explore more," Iyer said in a video shared by BCCI.The India captain acknowledged the unfamiliarity surrounding the contest."It is going to be a thrilling and exciting match for us. This is the first time we would be playing Japan, and do not know much about the conditions, the wicket, but looking forward to have a great match," he added.The match also serves as India's final preparation before their Asian Games campaign, which begins on September 28 with a quarterfinal. India enter the fixture as the reigning T20 World Cup champions, while Japan are ranked 41st in the format. BCCI has confirmed the Japan match as part of India's build-up to the Asian Games.For Japan, meanwhile, the occasion represents a major milestone. The hosts will face one of the biggest names in international cricket on home soil, with Japan captain Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming insisting his side are not merely there to celebrate the occasion but to demonstrate what they can do.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship permutations: Warwickshire attempt to seal Division One title with Somerset and Nottinghamshire still in contention
articles.summary: Nottinghamshire lead Somerset and Nottinghamshire in a three-way battle for the County Championship Division One title going into the final round of fixtures; relegation from and promotion to the top tier are also still to be decided
articles.body:
Warwickshire are the clear favourites to claim the Division One title for the first time since 2021.

They begin the final round 11 points clear at the top of the table and know that victory at home over Leicestershire will confirm them as champions.

Warwickshire could also win the title if they draw or lose, depending on the results of second-placed Somerset and third-placed Nottinghamshire.

Somerset, who trail Warwickshire by 11 points, must win their home fixture against Surrey and hope that Warwickshire either draw and claim three fewer bonus points than them, or lose.

If Somerset won, Warwickshire drew and the sides were tied on points, Somerset would claim the title by having seven victories to Warwickshire's six.

Nottinghamshire go into the final round with only an outside chance as they sit 15 points back from Warwickshire.

They must beat Yorkshire at home but also need Warwickshire to lose and Somerset to draw or lose.

It's possible that Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire could finish tied on points with the same number of wins, losses and draws, which would see the title decided by which of the pair claimed more points in their two fixtures against each other this season.

That would be Nottinghamshire, who outpointed Warwickshire 27-24 by achieving more bonus scoring as the sides drew both of their clashes.

Leicestershire and Essex in battle for survival

With Hampshire's relegation from Division One already confirmed, Leicestershire and Essex are the other two sides at risk of going down.

Ninth-placed Leicestershire are 19 points behind eighth-placed Essex, which makes the former a heavy favourite to be relegated.

Leicestershire must achieve an upset victory over league leaders Warwickshire, and hope that Essex lose at Glamorgan.

Kent and Northamptonshire in tight promotion duel

Durham, helped by the presence of former England captain Ben Stokes, sealed promotion as Division Two champions with two games to spare.

However, the battle for the second promotion place is a thrilling one with Kent leading Northamptonshire by just four points going into their final fixtures.

Kent host bottom side Gloucestershire, while Northamptonshire are away to mid-table Middlesex at Lord's.

Given Kent have already sealed the tiebreaker between the sides because they have two more victories, Northamptonshire must outscore them by five points to be promoted.

That would be difficult to achieve in the event both sides won, so Northamptonshire are likely to need to better Kent's result to leapfrog them.

Gloucestershire do have some additional motivation to upset Kent, with the away side needing a victory, or draw with bonus points, to have a chance of getting off the bottom of the table.
